# DocumentedReturnType

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report a returned value that breaks the function's return contract when
PHPDoc is taken into account: the `@return` type rejects it, or the
declared return type rejects a value whose type only PHPDoc describes. PHP
may run such a `return`, but the code and its documentation disagree.
Mismatches the code alone proves are InvalidReturnType's.

## Example

```php{8,14}
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

class Order {}
/** @return Order */
function latest()
{
    return 'order-1';
}

/** @param string $amount */
function cents($amount): int
{
    return $amount;
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 8: Return Order from latest(), not string.</li>
<li>line 14: Return int from cents(), not string.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Returned values and the functions that own them as
  InvalidReturnType defines them.
- The type of the value is the one PHPDoc-aware inference gives:
  `@param`, `@var` and `@return` tags count.
- The declared return type or the function's own `@return` type
  (`@phpstan-return` and `@psalm-return` first) accepts no value of the
  value's type. `$this` in a `@return` type accepts nothing that the
  declaring class rejects.
- Integer ranges, string lengths and literal values of the `@return`
  type count only against a value whose possible values are all known
  (an integer literal such as `-1`, the count of a literal array) or, for
  a string, whose values or byte lengths are (a string literal such as
  `''` or `'gone'`); otherwise `@return positive-int` accepts any integer
  and `@return 'open'|'closed'` any string.
- The weak-mode conversions and the exceptions of InvalidReturnType
  apply alike.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Values InvalidReturnType reports: the declared type rejects what the
  code alone shows.
- A `@return` type naming a template, a conditional `@return` type,
  and a `@return` type the declared type rejects (a stale tag).
- A `@return` type the method does not write itself: inherited from a
  parent declaration, or through `{@inheritDoc}`.
- Every exception of InvalidReturnType.

## Fix

None: either the code or the documentation is wrong.

## PHP versions

All versions.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DocumentedReturnType": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DocumentedReturnType
```
